annotations.description: Jack-o'-Lantern is actually the best card to discard here for this deck's strategy. The Poxwalkers return from the graveyard whenever you cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand, so discarding a Poxwalkers would effectively not lose a card - it would set up the recursive engine. The reasoning given was completely wrong (calling Jack-o'-Lantern a '1/1 creature' when it's an artifact), but the actual choice of discarding Jack-o'-Lantern over Poxwalkers is a minor missed opportunity. Discarding a Poxwalkers would put it in the graveyard ready to be recurred, while Jack-o'-Lantern can at least be exiled from the graveyard for mana. However, the Poxwalkers synergy with the self-mill/combo plan makes discarding one of them clearly better.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Poxwalkers, which can return from the graveyard to the battlefield when spells are cast from non-hand zones, effectively making it free to discard and setting up the recursive engine.

annotations.description: With Bayou and Ignoble Hierarch available (producing BG and B/R/G respectively), Libby has access to BG mana, which is exactly what Wight of the Reliquary costs. Wight is a 2/2 with vigilance that grows with creatures in the graveyard (currently 4 creature cards: Ignoble Hierarch, Grist the Hunger Tide which counts as a creature in graveyard, and potentially others depending on exact graveyard contents). With 4 creatures in graveyard (Ignoble Hierarch, Grist), Wight would be at least a 4/4. Additionally, Wight can sacrifice creatures to tutor lands, providing both board presence and utility. Birds of Paradise is a 0/1 mana dork that adds one mana of any color - useful but much less impactful than a large threat. Alternatively, Badgermole Cub costs 1G and provides a 2/2 body plus earthbend (animating a land as a creature with a +1/+1 counter) plus the mana-doubling ability with Ignoble Hierarch. However, Wight of the Reliquary is likely the strongest play here as it puts significant pressure on the board immediately as a large creature. Playing Birds of Paradise when you could deploy a meaningful threat is a tempo loss.
